newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel eyeing muni amendments to tax bill.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel eyeing muni amendments to tax bill.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Finance Committee could act on as many as nine proposed revisions to a broad tax package that would affect the muni bond market, a 12-page summary of draft amendments says.
At 1750 EDT, the panel remained in a closed caucus deciding how many of a total of 114 proposed revisions to Chairman William Roth's tax package should be brought up for a vote later tonight.
Florida Democrat Bob Graham said he wants to offer five amendments to simplify the tax code for municipal bond issuers, according to the list. His revisions would:
* Increase the small arbitrage rebate exemption to $25 million for certain education facilities;
* Provide a simplified three-year safe harbor for exemption from the arbitrage rebate rules for financing certain facilities. The proposal does not specify education projects;
* Exclude up to $25 million in construction of certain education facilities from the $10 million limit on the amount of bonds a government may issue annually;
* Create a category of exempt facility bonds for certain education facilities and make it subject to a separate cap on bond volume equal to $10 per capita annually; and
* Modify depreciation rules to allow tax-exempt financed education facilities to receive accelerated depreciation.
Sen. Kent Conrad, a Democrat from North Dakota, wants to offer an amendment liberalizing "mortgage bond eligibility rules" for financings in areas declared disasters by the President.
And Sen. Frank Murkowski, R-Alaska, chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, backs a proposal to allow advance refunding of tax-exempt Virgin Island bonds.
Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun, D-Ill., is calling for a tax credit for school infrastructure projects, to be offset with an increase in the tobacco tax.
Braun also is calling for designation of two additional urban empowerment zones. And she wants to expand the definition of "brownfields."
Tax-exempt financing is a feature in both of these federal programs.
